<STRUCT_0001>
An important reason to study flat morphisms is that they provide the adequate
framework for capturing the notion of a family of schemes parametrized by the
points of another scheme. Naively one may think that any morphism <MATH_0001>
should be thought of as a family parametrized by the points of <MATH_0002>. However,
without a flatness restriction on <MATH_0003>, really bizarre things can happen in
this so-called family. For instance, we aren't guaranteed that relative
dimension (dimension of the fibres) is constant in a family. Other numerical
invariants, such as the Hilbert polynomial, too may change from fibre to
fibre. Flatness prevents such things from happening and, therefore, provides
some ``continuity'' to the fibres.

<STRUCT_0001>
In this section, we will define <ACCENT_0001>tale morphisms and prove a number of
important properties about them. The most important one, no doubt, is the
functorial characterization presented in Theorem <REF_0001>.
Following this, we will also discuss a few properties of rings which are
insensitive to an <ACCENT_0002>tale extension (properties which hold for a ring
if and only if they hold for all its <ACCENT_0003>tale extensions) to motivate the basic
tenet of <ACCENT_0004>tale cohomology -- <ACCENT_0005>tale morphisms are the algebraic analogue of
local isomorphisms.

An important reason to study flat morphisms is that they provide the adequate
framework for capturing the notion of a family of schemes parametrized by the
points of another scheme. Naively one may think that any morphism <MATH_0001>
should be thought of as a family parametrized by the points of <MATH_0002>. However,
without a flatness restriction on <MATH_0003>, really bizarre things can happen in
this so-called family. For instance, we aren't guaranteed that relative
dimension (dimension of the fibres) is constant in a family. Other numerical
invariants, such as the Hilbert polynomial, too may change from fibre to
fibre. Flatness prevents such things from happening and, therefore, provides
some ``continuity'' to the fibres.

if and only if they hold for all its <ACCENT_0003>tale extensions) to motivate the basic
tenet of <ACCENT_0004>tale cohomology -- <ACCENT_0005>tale morphisms are the algebraic analogue of
local isomorphisms.
